findings.mechanism: Replace/shared dense update paths with sparsely accessed memory layers and update only memory slots that are highly specific to the new batch relative to pretraining usage (TF-IDF-style slot ranking), leaving general/shared slots frozen.
findings.quantitative_evidence: On a stream of TriviaQA facts with matched new-knowledge acquisition, NaturalQuestions F1 reportedly dropped 89% under full finetuning, 71% under LoRA, and only 11% under sparse memory finetuning. The work also evaluates a streamed-document SimpleQA setting and reports the same qualitative Pareto advantage.
findings.evidence_scope: 2025 Meta FAIR/UC Berkeley preprint on a 1.3B memory-layer language model, two QA continual-learning settings, with held-out NaturalQuestions/GSM8K forgetting probes. This is strong primary quantitative evidence but is not yet treated as peer-reviewed evidence here.
findings.decision_relevance: Potentially important if O eventually performs persistent parametric learning: it supports architectural localization of plasticity instead of global/shared updates. Conceptually it complements O's selective Context Kernel, but it is a distinct parameter-update mechanism and should be matched against simpler external-memory/context-only alternatives before adoption.

findings.quantitative_evidence: Continual Bench Table 1 reports model-based final average performance/regret (%): fine-tuning 24.86/37.74, SI 39.96/33.57, Coreset 61.83/30.83, Perfect Memory 73.09/30.95, and OA 72.93/27.62. OA therefore approximately matches Perfect Memory average performance while achieving lower regret, without an unbounded replay buffer; the paper states its incremental update has constant overhead in the studied formulation.
findings.evidence_scope: Six-task Continual Bench model-based planning setting with shared dynamics and reward changes. The numeric superiority should not be generalized beyond this environment/model class; the paper itself notes moderate-dimensional state-space limitations.
findings.decision_relevance: This strengthens priority for a matched architectural test of 'shared world model + planning' versus continually rewriting task-specific policies when the environment dynamics are shared.

next_queries: Find peer-reviewed follow-up or independent replication of sparse memory finetuning / memory-layer localized updates.
Compare sparse memory finetuning with pure external retrieval under matched knowledge acquisition and inference cost.
Find agent-scale experiments where only a world model or memory component remains plastic while the policy/base LLM stays fixed.
Search for task-compatibility scoring that predicts whether a memory item should be replayed, extending the harmful-replay result into an actionable selector.

continuation.frontier: Highest-value mechanisms now form a coherent hypothesis family: localize plasticity (world model, sparse memory slots, or selected replay) while keeping broad shared behavior stable, and evaluate interference rather than assuming more replay/context is safer. Next seek independent/peer-reviewed replication and direct agent/LLM transfer evidence.
